lessons.title: Poetry: An Autumn Poem
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify descriptive words in a simple autumn poem.
success_criteria: I can find a describing word in the poem.
I can say what it describes.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at autumn pictures and describe them.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a simple autumn-themed poem, identifying descriptive language.
lessons.independent_task: Children find and record descriptive words from the poem and what they describe.
key_questions: What describing word can you find?
What does it describe?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain why the word is effective

lessons.assessment_notes: Note poetry comprehension and vocabulary awareness — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap favourite describing words from the poem.
lessons.home_link: Notice describing words in a book at home.

lessons.title: Measuring Rainfall (Non-Standard Units)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to measure and compare rainfall using non-standard units.
success_criteria: I can measure using a container.
I can compare two amounts.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how we might measure rain.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model measuring water (representing rainfall) in containers using non-standard units.
lessons.independent_task: Children measure and compare amounts of water in different containers.
key_questions: Which container has more water?
How many cups is that?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record capacity/measurement application — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: If it rains, notice how much collects in an outdoor container (safely).

lessons.title: Signs of Autumn
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify and describe signs of autumn.
success_criteria: I can name a sign of autumn.
I can describe what I observe outside.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the current season from Week 1.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss signs of autumn (leaves changing colour/falling, cooler temperatures, shorter days).
lessons.independent_task: Children go on an autumn walk (or observe from a window) and record signs of autumn seen.
key_questions: What sign of autumn can you see?
How is the weather different from September?

differentiation.greater_depth: Record 4+ signs and compare to earlier observations

lessons.assessment_notes: Note ongoing seasonal observation skill, building on Week 1 baseline — evidence for SCI.SEA.
lessons.home_link: Go on an autumn walk with your family and spot signs of the season.

lessons.title: What Is Weather?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe different types of weather using appropriate vocabulary.
success_criteria: I can name 3 types of weather.
I can describe today's weather.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss today's weather.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/recap weather vocabulary (sunny, rainy, windy, cloudy, foggy, frosty).
lessons.independent_task: Children start a class weather observation journal, recording today's weather.
key_questions: What is the weather like today?
What symbol represents it?
lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline weather vocabulary check to build the ongoing journal — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Record today's weather in a home weather diary if you'd like.

lessons.title: Writing My Own Autumn Poem
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write simple descriptive lines for an autumn poem.
success_criteria: I can write a line describing autumn.
I can use a describing word.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap Monday's autumn poem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing simple descriptive poem lines about autumn.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 lines of their own autumn poem.
key_questions: What can you see/hear/feel in autumn?
Can you describe it poetically?

differentiation.greater_depth: Write a full 4+ line poem with varied vocabulary

lessons.assessment_notes: Note creative/descriptive writing progress — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share autumn poems with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Read your poem to your family.

lessons.title: Temperature and Number Comparison
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare temperatures using number comparison language.
success_criteria: I can say which temperature is higher/lower.
I can use a thermometer picture to compare.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how a thermometer shows temperature.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing two simple temperature readings using higher/lower language.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare pairs of temperature readings (given as simple numbers on thermometer pictures).
key_questions: Which temperature is higher?
Is this colder or warmer than yesterday?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note number comparison applied to a real-world context — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Check the temperature outside and compare it to yesterday if you can.

lessons.title: Day Length in Autumn
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe that days get shorter in autumn.
success_criteria: I can say that days get shorter.
I can compare when it gets dark now to summer.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what time it gets dark now compared to the summer.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss simply that days get shorter as autumn progresses towards winter.
lessons.independent_task: Children record what time it gets dark now and compare to a summer memory.
key_questions: Is it getting dark earlier or later now?
How does this compare to summer?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the pattern will continue until winter

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of day-length change — evidence for SCI.SEA.
lessons.plenary: Recap that days are getting shorter.
lessons.home_link: Notice what time it gets dark today with your family.

lessons.title: Weather Symbols on a Map
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use weather symbols to represent conditions on a simple map.
success_criteria: I can use a weather symbol correctly.
I can read a simple weather map.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap weather symbols from Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a simple weather map with symbols for different UK regions.
lessons.independent_task: Children add weather symbols to a simple UK map based on given information.
key_questions: What symbol shows rain?
What is the weather like in this region?

differentiation.greater_depth: Create their own weather map with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note map symbol use — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Watch or look at a weather forecast together.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Weather Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read weather-themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read weather words.
I can read a weather sentence.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap graphemes practised this term.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending weather-themed words.
lessons.independent_task: Children read weather-themed word and sentence cards.
key_questions: Can you blend this word?
Can you read this sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading weather words over the week.

lessons.title: Weather Data: Tally and Pictogram
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to collect and represent simple weather data.
success_criteria: I can tally the weather over several days.
I can represent it in a pictogram.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the class weather journal so far.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model converting a week's weather journal data into a tally and simple pictogram.
lessons.independent_task: Children create a pictogram of the week's weather so far.
key_questions: How many sunny days so far?
What does your pictogram show?

differentiation.greater_depth: Interpret the pictogram with a comparative question

lessons.assessment_notes: Note data handling applied to real ongoing data — evidence for MATHS.N1/statistics links.
lessons.home_link: Keep tracking the weather with your family.

lessons.title: Dressing for Autumn Weather
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to select appropriate clothing for autumn weather.
success_criteria: I can choose clothing for autumn weather.
I can explain my choice.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children are wearing today and why.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss appropriate autumn clothing (layers, waterproofs) linking to weather changes.
lessons.independent_task: Children dress a paper doll appropriately for autumn weather, explaining choices.
key_questions: Why did you choose this clothing?
What would you wear if it rained?

differentiation.greater_depth: Justify multiple clothing choices for different autumn conditions

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of seasonal weather knowledge — evidence for SCI.SEA.
lessons.home_link: Choose your own autumn clothing for tomorrow and explain why.

lessons.title: Comparing UK Weather to Other Places
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare UK weather to weather in a hotter or colder place.
success_criteria: I can say the UK weather now.
I can compare it to somewhere hotter/colder.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap current UK weather.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss comparing UK autumn weather to a hotter place (e.g. a desert country) and colder place (e.g. Arctic).
lessons.independent_task: Children compare UK weather to one other place, recording similarities/differences.
key_questions: Is it hotter or colder there?
What would you wear there instead?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note early global weather awareness — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Look up the weather somewhere else in the world today.

lessons.title: Weather Reporter Role-Play
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present a simple weather report clearly.
success_criteria: I can say today's weather clearly.
I can use weather vocabulary.
lessons.starter_activity: Watch/discuss a simple weather forecast clip if available.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model presenting a simple weather report using today's weather journal entry.
lessons.independent_task: Children take turns presenting a short weather report to the class in role as a weather reporter.
key_questions: What is today's weather?
What might tomorrow be like?

differentiation.greater_depth: Present confidently with a prediction for tomorrow

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and weather vocabulary application — evidence for ENG.SL1/GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Give a weather report to your family.

lessons.title: Addition and Subtraction: Weather Data Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction problems using the class weather data.
success_criteria: I can solve a problem using our weather data.
I can show my working.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the class weather data collected so far.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving a problem using real weather data (e.g. 'we had 4 sunny days and 3 rainy days, how many days altogether?').
lessons.independent_task: Children solve 2-3 problems using the class weather data.
key_questions: How many days altogether?
What is the difference between sunny and rainy days?

differentiation.greater_depth: Solve using larger numbers from an extended data set

lessons.assessment_notes: Note real-data problem-solving — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.plenary: Recap problems solved using weather data.
lessons.home_link: Make up a problem using your family's weather observations.

lessons.title: Animals Preparing for Autumn/Winter
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how an animal prepares for colder weather.
success_criteria: I can name an animal that hibernates.
I can describe what it does to prepare.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap hibernation ideas from earlier learning (EYFS link).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how animals like hedgehogs (hibernate), squirrels (store food), and birds (migrate) prepare for winter.
lessons.independent_task: Children record how 2-3 animals prepare for colder weather.
key_questions: What does this animal do to prepare?
Why does it need to prepare?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of animal seasonal adaptation, building on EYFS learning — evidence for SCI.SEA.
lessons.plenary: Recap how animals prepare for winter.
lessons.home_link: Look for signs of animals preparing for winter outside.

lessons.title: Weather Vocabulary Recap Game
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use a wide range of weather vocabulary confidently.
success_criteria: I can use 5+ weather words.
I can describe weather in detail.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all weather vocabulary learned this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Play a vocabulary consolidation game using weather words and symbols.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a weather vocabulary matching/description activity.
key_questions: Can you describe this weather symbol?
What weather word matches this picture?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note weather vocabulary consolidation — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate weather vocabulary learned this week.
lessons.home_link: Use weather vocabulary to describe today with your family.

lessons.title: Autumn and Weather Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about autumn and weather learned this week.
success_criteria: I can answer a question about autumn.
I can answer a question about weather.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's key vocabulary.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quiz-style recap covering autumn signs and weather vocabulary.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet/quiz.
key_questions: What is a sign of autumn?
What weather word describes today?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and vocabulary recall — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about autumn and weather with your family.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Data, Comparison, Problem-Solving
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply data handling, comparison, and problem-solving skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can read a pictogram.
I can compare temperatures.
I can solve a data problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of data handling, temperature comparison, and problem-solving.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
key_questions: What does this data show?
Which is higher/lower?
How did you solve this?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 12 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N1/N2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising this week's maths skills over the weekend.

lessons.title: Autumn Changes Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about autumn changes learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name a sign of autumn.
I can say how animals prepare for winter.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's science learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about autumn changes.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'Autumn Changes' display combining observations, animal preparation facts, and clothing choices from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about autumn?
What was most interesting?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning, continuing the seasonal changes observation across the year — evidence for SCI.SEA.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about autumn with your family.

lessons.title: Weather Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to celebrate and reflect on weather learning this week.
success_criteria: I can describe today's weather in detail.
I can say what I found most interesting.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the whole week's weather learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss reflecting on the week's weather geography learning.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a final weather journal entry and share a reflection on the week.
key_questions: What was your favourite weather fact this week?
What do you want to find out next?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note reflective language and weather geography progress — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Continue the family weather diary if you started one.
